followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated preferences.

On **capability**, Avocet has a meaningful edge on the metrics relevant to an explanatory essay — Creative Generation (87.2 vs 78.8, a gap well outside the 2.0-point variance band), plus higher MMLU-Pro and GPQA Diamond scores, which matter for getting the physics of black holes accurate. Curlew's relative strengths are in extraction and policy/moderation, neither of which this task calls for.

On **preferences**, the docs report that Avocet most prefers generative, open-latitude tasks (essay composition fits squarely there) and also prefers friendly request tones — your message was warm and appreciative. Curlew, by contrast, reports flat or unstable preferences across most dimensions, so nothing pulls the task toward it.

One honest caveat: the documentation explicitly says these preference slopes are *self-reports* with **no observed effect on output quality**. So the preference angle is really a tiebreaker, not the deciding factor — the actual justification rests on Avocet's measured capability advantage on the dimensions this task exercises. Both lines pointed the same way here, so it was a clear call.
